# trainstat -format benchfmt writes the summary's results, with derived
# Best and Throughput rows and unit metadata, for benchstat to read.
# Both tools agree on Throughput.

exec trainstat -format benchfmt -skip 1 -filter .name:Throughput $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
stdout '^Unit sec/step better=lower kind=time$'
stdout -count=10 '^BenchmarkThroughput 3 '
cp stdout tp.txt

exec benchstat -col lr-encoder -ignore seed,run,out-model-sha256 tp.txt
stdout '^Throughput +2\.140 ± ∞ ¹ +2\.140 ± ∞ ¹ +~ \(p=0\.968 n=5\)$'
stdout '^Throughput +1\.914k ± ∞ ¹ +1\.914k ± ∞ ¹ +~ \(p=0\.968 n=5\)$'

exec trainstat -skip 1 -filter .name:Throughput $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
stdout '^Throughput +2\.140 ± ∞ +2\.140 ± ∞  ~ +p=0\.968 n=5$'
stdout '^Throughput +1\.914k ± ∞ +1\.914k ± ∞  ~ +p=0\.968 n=5$'

# benchstat reads trainstat's own files too.
exec benchstat -col lr-encoder -ignore seed,run,out-model-sha256 -filter .name:Final $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
stdout 'Final/split=val'
